overview: China is a country in East Asia and one of the two most populous countries in the world. Its capital is Beijing, and its largest city is Shanghai. China has one of the world's oldest continuous civilisations, and paper, printing, the compass and gunpowder were all invented there. It has been ruled by the Communist Party since 1949, and today it has the second-largest economy in the world.

geography.text: China's land falls from west to east. In the south-west, the Tibetan Plateau, the highest plateau on Earth, is bordered by the Himalayas, including Mount Everest on the border with Nepal. The north and west have deserts such as the Gobi and the Taklamakan, while most people live in the fertile east, along great rivers such as the Yellow River and the Yangtze, the longest river in Asia.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Everything from Siberian cold in the north-east to tropical heat in the south and dry deserts in the west.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Giant pandas, golden snub-nosed monkeys, and the South China tiger.

history.text: China's history stretches back thousands of years through a series of dynasties, beginning with the first unification under the Qin in 221 BC, when the first emperor joined up earlier walls into a Great Wall. The last emperor was overthrown in 1912. After a civil war, the Communist Party founded the People's Republic in 1949. Since economic reforms began in 1978, China has become the world's second-largest economy.

events.title: Mongol rule
events.text: Kublai Khan founds the Yuan dynasty.

events.title: Opium War
events.text: Britain fights China over the opium trade and takes Hong Kong.

events.title: People's Republic
events.text: Mao Zedong proclaims the People's Republic of China.

events.title: Economic reform
events.text: Deng Xiaoping begins opening up the economy.

government.text: China is a one-party state ruled by the Communist Party of China. The party's General Secretary is the most powerful person in the country and also serves as President. Xi Jinping has held these posts since 2012–13, and term limits on the presidency were removed in 2018. The National People's Congress passes laws but follows party decisions.

economy.text: China has the second-largest economy in the world and is the world's biggest manufacturer and exporter. It makes most of the world's phones, solar panels, batteries and electric vehicles, and it is also the largest trading partner of many countries. Since economic reforms began in 1978, hundreds of millions of people have been lifted out of poverty.

culture.text: China has one of the oldest continuous civilisations. It invented paper, printing, gunpowder and the compass. Mandarin Chinese has more native speakers than any other language. Chinese New Year, festivals, calligraphy, tea and kung fu are known around the world.

items.title: The Great Wall
items.text: Walls built over 2,000 years, stretching thousands of kilometres.

items.title: Terracotta Army
items.text: Thousands of life-size clay soldiers buried with the first emperor.

items.title: Four great inventions
items.text: Paper, printing, gunpowder and the compass.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Every region has its own style: spicy Sichuan food, dim sum from Guangdong and Peking duck.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: Calligraphy, Beijing opera, porcelain and the guqin, an ancient zither.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: Chinese New Year, or Spring Festival, brings red lanterns, dumplings, fireworks and the biggest yearly journey home in the world.

sport.text: China is a sporting superpower. It hosted the Summer Olympics in 2008 and the Winter Olympics in 2022, making Beijing the first city to host both. Table tennis, badminton, diving and gymnastics are its strongest sports, and basketball is hugely popular.

items.text: Beijing: the first city to host both Summer and Winter Olympics.

items.title: Table tennis
items.text: China has won most Olympic table tennis golds since 1988.

items.title: Yao Ming

didYouKnow: China uses only one time zone, even though it is as wide as the continental United States.
Giant pandas are found in the wild only in China.

keyPeople.name: Confucius
keyPeople.text: His teachings shaped Chinese society for over 2,000 years.
